belief: I'll end up completely dependent on others.
origins: Progressive vision or hearing loss raises a fear of losing independence completely. The fear can be worse than reality, and it can keep us from planning and using helpful tools.
teaches: “Do not worry about your life” (Matthew 6:25). “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.” “Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray.” Many people with sight or hearing loss live independently with training and tools. Learning skills now, such as orientation and mobility training, assistive technology, and communication strategies, can preserve independence. And if you do need more help someday, you will still be valued and loved.
self_statements: I will not be able to cope.
errors: Believing I will be either fully independent or fully dependent.
Feeling afraid and concluding that it will happen.
questions: What does my specialist say about my likely course?
What training or tools could help me stay independent?
What do I do well now?
Whom can I talk to who has adapted?
What does Scripture say about God carrying me?
truth: I can learn skills and use tools that keep me independent for as long as possible, and plan wisely. If I need more help, God will carry me and people will love me.
hw_truths: I do not worry about tomorrow.
log: Each month, note one skill or plan you made.
prayer: Lord, I fear losing independence. Carry me, give me wise tools and teachers, and keep me at peace whatever comes. Amen.
